facts.raw_span: 2-week history of vegetating, bleeding plaques and pustules on his face, scalp, trunk, and extremities
Lesions began as pustules and developed into painful, itchy plaques
Pustules and hemorrhagic-crusted plaques were seen on the scalp, legs, arms, and trunk along with keloidal plaques on the face
difficulty walking due to skin lesions
Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay testing for HIV was negative
Punch biopsy from arm showed: Epidermal hyperplasia and exocytosis of neutrophils
Dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration
Microabscesses scattered with eosinophils
No granulomas or multinucleated giant cells
Negative periodic acid–Schiff staining
Extensive vegetative plaques with bleeding and ulceration
Pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia (hematoxylin-eosin stain)

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques and pustules, along with the histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia, dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, and microabscesses, is consistent with Pyoderma Gangrenosum.
The patient's symptoms and histopathological findings, including the presence of microabscesses and dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, are also consistent with Sweet Syndrome.
Although less likely, the patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques and pustules, along with the negative periodic acid-Schiff staining, could also be consistent with Eczema Herpeticum.
The patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques and pustules could also be consistent with Impetigo, although the histopathological findings are not as supportive.
The patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques and pustules could also be consistent with Psoriasis, although the histopathological findings are not as supportive.
The patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques and pustules could also be consistent with Dermatitis, although the histopathological findings are not as supportive.

The patient's symptoms of vegetating, bleeding plaques and pustules, and the histopathology results showing epidermal hyperplasia and exocytosis of neutrophils, are consistent with Pyodermatitis-Pyostomatitis Vegetans, which is a rare skin condition.

rationales.F01: The presence of vegetating, bleeding plaques and pustules is more typical of Pyoderma Gangrenosum and Pyodermatitis-Pyostomatitis Vegetans.
rationales.F06: Epidermal hyperplasia and exocytosis of neutrophils are characteristic of Pyoderma Gangrenosum and Sweet Syndrome.
rationales.F07: Dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration is characteristic of Pyoderma Gangrenosum and Sweet Syndrome.
rationales.F08: Microabscesses scattered with eosinophils are characteristic of Pyoderma Gangrenosum and Sweet Syndrome.
rationales.F12: Pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia is characteristic of Pyoderma Gangrenosum and Pyodermatitis-Pyostomatitis Vegetans.
